subject: Response: Third-Party & Cloud Provider Assurance — BluePeak RFP BP-4832
messages:
From: Alice Brown <alice.brown@bluepeak.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@bluepeak.com
Date: Tue, 07 Apr 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: BluePeak RFP#BP-4832 — Third-party inventory and cloud assurance

Vanessa,

Thanks for taking our RFP. As part of our security review we need an up-to-date inventory of all third-party vendors and subprocessors Redwood currently uses for the hosted API and dedicated offerings. Specifically we need:

- A spreadsheet listing vendor name, purpose (eg. monitoring, storage, KMS), hosting location/region, and whether they have access to customer data.
- Copies or references to your cloud provider assurances (SOC 2 / ISO attestation links or summary), and the names of the cloud regions used for production data for hosted customers.
- Your standard change-notice policy for adding/removing subprocessors and required notice windows for customers (both standard and enterprise).
- Whether Redwood supports customer-managed encryption keys (KMS) and any constraints around that for Private/Dedicated deployments.

We would like the inventory in CSV/XLSX and the policy as a PDF. Timelines: procurement would like these items by end-of-week (Friday) to stay on track for next-week evaluations.

RFP reference: BP-4832

Appreciate it,

Alice Brown
Sr. Procurement Manager — BluePeak Financial
alice.brown@bluepeak.com
procurement@bluepeak.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alice Brown <alice.brown@bluepeak.com>
Cc: procurement@bluepeak.com
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 10:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BluePeak RFP#BP-4832 — Third-party inventory and cloud assurance

Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. Please find attached an export of our current third-party inventory and our change-notice policy. High-level answers up front:

- Inventory: attached spreadsheet (redwood_thirdparty_inventory_2026-04-09.xlsx) includes vendor name, role, data access field, primary region(s), and attestations where available. Key entries: AWS (S3, EKS) — us-east-1 / us-west-2; GCP (replication for EU customers) — europe-west1; Azure used for on-prem integration tests. Monitoring/telemetry: Datadog (no plaintext customer data retained). KMS: Customer-managed KMS is available for Private deployments; hosted customers can request CMK options under enterprise contracts.

- Attestations: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II (scope: production runtime, infra ops). We publish a summary and can share the full report under NDA. We also have vendor-level attestations referenced in the inventory where vendors publish them.

- Change-notice policy: Standard policy is in the attached PDF (change_notice_policy.pdf). In short: additions that are non-security-impacting — 30 days advance notice; security-critical updates or urgent vendor patches — we notify within 48 hours and provide mitigation details. Decommission/migration windows are 60 days for standard customers.

- KMS/Encryption: Data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). For Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or HSM integrations). Key separation and BYOK options are documented in the migration runbook attached.

Attachments in this email: redwood_thirdparty_inventory_2026-04-09.xlsx (spreadsheet), change_notice_policy.pdf, migration_runbook_v1.1.pdf

If you want a separate spreadsheet filtered to only vendors that could have access to customer plaintext (e.g., support integrations, on-call access), I can produce that slice. We can also schedule a technical call to walk through the runbook if your security team prefers.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: BluePeak RFP#BP-4832 — internal: legal/security asks

Vanessa / Rishi —

Quick internal note after reviewing BluePeak's RFP language and their initial ask: Legal is pushing for a 90-day minimum notification window for any change that could materially affect customer data locality or cloud provider choice (they flagged language in the procurement template). Security has two asks:

- Clarify how cross-region replication is configured for hosted customers and whether keys are region-bound.
- Confirm that monitoring vendors (Datadog) do not receive customer plaintext and have only hashed/tokenized IDs where possible.

My read: our public policy (30/60/48) is fine for most customers, but we should offer a contract-level option to extend the decommission/migration window to 90 days for enterprise accounts (BP-4832 is a good candidate). Can Rishi confirm whether there are any technical blockers to committing to 90 days for Dedicated/Private deployments?

I also attached the procurement clause they shared (procurement_clause_BP-4832.docx) for context. If Legal wants the SOC 2 report, we should plan to share under NDA only.

Thanks — Priyom

Subject: Re: BluePeak RFP#BP-4832 — Third-party inventory and cloud assurance

Alice —

Appreciate the patience while we coordinated internally. We've updated the inventory and policy to reflect the enterprise options you asked about. Summary of what we can commit to for BluePeak under a standard enterprise amendment: 

- Notification windows: Standard customers: 60 days for decommission/migration; 30 days for non-critical additions; 48 hours for security-critical notices. For enterprise customers with a signed amendment, Redwood will commit to a 90-day advance notification for changes that materially affect cloud provider choice, data locality, or any vendor that could access customer plaintext.

- Migration support: For enterprise customers we provide an assigned technical lead and a migration runbook. We will schedule a joint technical run and dry-run at no additional charge during the first migration engagement. See attached migration_runbook_v1.2.pdf.

- KMS and key separation: We support customer-managed keys for Private/Dedicated deployments (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM options). Hosted customers can opt into CMK under an enterprise contract. Keys are region-aware; cross-region replication for backups can be configured per-customer and documented in the runbook.

- Attestations: We will share the SOC 2 Type II report under NDA; vendor attestations are listed in the attached inventory.

Next steps I propose:
1) I attached an updated inventory (redwood_thirdparty_inventory_2026-04-11.xlsx) and a revised change-notice policy (change_notice_policy_v2.pdf) that includes the enterprise 90-day option.
2) If BluePeak agrees, we can add the 90-day notification clause as a simple amendment to the MSA (I can loop Legal). HubSpot deal ID: BP-4832.
3) Schedule a technical onboarding call — I included a link to a shared Drive with the artifacts and a DocuSign link to sign an amendment when you're ready.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Redwood/bluepeak-rfp-BP-4832
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/link/reds-amen-4832

Please let me know if you'd like the SOC 2 immediately — we can send it under NDA. Happy to hop on a 30-minute call this week to walk your security team through the runbook.

Thanks,

Vanessa Ortiz
